## New features
- **Live receptor levels follow receptor drags on slow models.** Moving a receptor now re-solves only that receptor's stack and keeps every other level, with identical numbers. On P1987 (three CRTN roads) each step takes about 2 s instead of 14 s. A change too slow to follow while you edit (moving a building on that model, for example) is skipped with a note in the status bar; live levels no longer switch off for the whole project.
- **Results says when a run is out of date.** When the model or calculation method has changed since the run on screen, a note above the table says so, as the Contours tab already does, so older levels are not reported by mistake.

## Changes
- The contours side panel hides a section whose controls do not apply to the chosen method (Labels for Interpolated Raster showed a bare heading).
- Scale bars put the last number on its tick with the unit after it, so "25 m" no longer crowds "20".
- The Inputs table spells out heights and thicknesses, and lists a building's courtyards only when it has some.
- Reflection order sensitivity has compact captioned fields and Run comparison as its main action; Scenario Manager marks the active scenario in bold and uses the usual teal for Save Changes.

## Bug fixes
- Results showed an empty table under "24 receptors · dB" after opening a project whose saved runs came from an earlier version (12 of 19 real projects checked). Those runs list their receptors and levels again.
- Switching the time slice (Day to Night, say) made a current Day + Night run count as out of date: the report basis asked for a recalculation before issue, and reopening the project did not restore its levels.
- SmartSmooth no longer builds face meshes in parallel that it is bound to discard: a face without calculated support (a grid older than its buildings) used to send all the parallel work to waste, and one face that could not be meshed abandoned the others.
- Some fixed-height fields (Settings rows, dialog number boxes) could still grow to the stylesheet's taller minimum.
